tools.name: ci
tools.desc: Pushes your local commits and runs the repository's fast CI on the commit; where the project runs its CI on demand, it runs only what you name: the tests you list, and the checks you name. When it is done, it gives you the result of each check and of each test you listed, and puts in your worktree, uncommitted, the files a red run generated that differ from yours, such as the files as the formatter makes them. The full CI, every check and every test, runs once, at the merge
tools.runs: The engine checks the request and the head, telling everything wrong with them at once, and pushes. On the first push of a commit beyond main it opens a draft PR with the title and description handed in, and updates them when new ones come; GitHub opens none for a branch with no commit beyond main, so a push of such a branch opens none and only runs the fast CI. Where the project's configuration has its CI run on demand (on_demand), the push runs nothing: the engine runs the fast CI workflow the configuration names on the branch by hand with the tests listed, which runs those tests, each to its end, and the checks named, among those the configuration lists (named_checks), given by the input it names (checks_input), and it takes only the run it made, never one made before; a job the run skipped, as the lint when it is not named, is not among the checks it gives. When no test is listed and no check named, it runs nothing and gives no check. Otherwise the push runs the fast CI workflow, the whole of it, which stops a job at its first red test. GitHub runs a workflow by hand on a branch by the file of it the branch holds; where it refuses to, as on a branch made before main's workflow took the request, and main's CI files (.github/) differ from the branch's, the engine runs it on a temporary ref holding the head with main's CI files, those the work changed itself kept as the work has them, gives that run as the head's and deletes the ref. The engine waits for the run to finish and downloads the logs of red checks. When tests are listed, it downloads the results the run reported, JUnit XML in the artifact the configuration names (`project.ci.results`), and reads from them what became of each test each listed name names and how long it took; a test the run did not reach is not run. When the run is red and uploaded the artifact of generated files the configuration names (generated_artifact), such as the files as the formatter makes them, it writes those that differ from the worktree's into it

tools.name: ci_before
tools.desc: Runs the tests you list on the code before the change: the engine puts these tests' files on the code before the change, runs them, and gives you the result of each check and of each test. Nothing goes onto this work's branch. Only files in the test paths go there: a test written in a file of the implementation cannot, since that file's change is the change itself, so write it in a file of its own in the test paths. A test that cannot run on the code before the change, as one that needs what only the change adds to be built or to reach what it tests, is not run there: say so where you report the test, and why, and the review judges it
tools.runs: The engine takes the listed files from the pushed head, puts them on the commit this work's branch forked from main, and commits that to a temporary branch. Where the project's fast CI takes the tests to run (its configuration's tests_input), the engine runs that workflow on the branch with the listed tests, which runs exactly them, each to its end. Otherwise the push runs the whole fast CI, which stops a job at its first red test, where the project's configuration says its CI runs on those branches (runs_on_before_branches, true unless set); where it says it does not, nothing is pushed, and the tool refuses, saying so. Where GitHub refuses to run the workflow by hand with the CI files (.github/) of the code before the change, as those of a branch made before main's took the request, and main's differ, the engine puts main's CI files on that code and runs it again. It waits for the run to finish, downloads the logs of red checks, deletes the temporary branch, and reads what became of each test each listed name names from the results the run reported, JUnit XML in the artifact the configuration names (`project.ci.results`). A unit of tests that could not be built on the code before the change, as one that uses what the change adds, is reported as not built, and the tests of every other unit still run

tools.desc: Puts the source of the dependencies one of the project's lock files locks, each package at the locked version as it was published (its types included), in a directory of your worktree for you to read. The lock file is read as the worktree has it, uncommitted changes included. A command that runs past its time limit (`timeout`, 600 seconds unless the configuration sets it) is stopped with everything it started, and one that ends leaves nothing it started running: what is left in its process group is stopped when it ends. steps.start_work: Has the session manager set up where the work runs and the engineer's session, on a machine with a free slot. An item worked on here before takes over its latest earlier work's branch, its worktree (reused when it is there, made afresh from the branch otherwise) and its PR; an item imported with a branch takes that branch and the PR imported with it; any other item gets a new branch from main.
steps.run_tools: Runs the tools the calling cell asked for, from the commits the session manager bundled. When the work comes back from the architect, it runs again only the tools that failed. A tool that fails is retried twice before it counts as failed.
steps.merge: Puts the PR in this repository's merge queue; at its turn, catches it up with main, runs the full CI once and merges it when it is green: the three one after another, the queue taking one work at a time. Where the project's CI runs on demand, the full CI on the head is a run made by hand now; the merge waits for a green run of the full CI, never for one of the fast CI, and a run without a check merging needs is red. A conflict or a red check goes back to the engineer, who fixes everything with the fast CI before the full CI runs again; the third time in a row it goes to the architect.
steps.ask_architect: Queues what is asked for the architect, starting a work of the architect when none runs; the engineer's work stops and waits without holding a slot. The architect answers with a reply, brought back unchanged.
steps.ask_owner: Puts what is asked before the owner, as an ask of the owner in the owner's interface, and notifies the owner. For the architect, the ask holds only the matter of the path that asked, and the architect's work goes on; the owner's chosen option or sentence goes back unchanged to the side that asked: for a held matter, when it is picked again, to the cell that asked. For an engineer's work, the work waits for the answer, holding no slot, and the answer goes back unchanged to the cell that asked: the engineer's question about what the owner wants, the owner's review of a design, or the owner's approval of a change.
steps.end_work: Ends the work as every work ends, and keeps its branch. A work whose whole item went to sub-items ends here without merging, and its item is done once the sub-items are merged.
steps.wait_for_matter: No work of the project's architect runs: the engine takes this cell's rows for each project whose architect runs none, without a round, and one that takes `due` gets a work of the architect's graph, on no item, which starts at the cell that row leads to. The work holds no slot, and one runs at a time for each project; once it ends, the project waits here again. The engine watches main's CI for every project first (`queue_main_red`).
steps.stop_architect_work: An architect's work that the flow version the engine runs cannot take on ends here, at once, as the row of the cell for a work on an older version brings it: the work records why it ended (the version it cannot go on in, and why), and a project's architect runs one work at a time, so that the next look starts a new one when a matter is due. Its asks of the owner stay the owner's to answer, the matters they hold coming back with the answer, and its project's hold of new starts for setting it straight stays while a place to set straight is left open.
steps.look_at_queue: Looks at the project's queue and the base, and takes what comes next in a fixed order, without a round, as facts decide and no agent: first a new base, when the project has none, the policy changed since the base, or what came since it reached the installation's amount (`architect.carried_most`); then the owner's words and the matters back with the owner's reply, the one that came first; then main's CI red; then the matter a work stopped at its question waits on, the reports of the returns sent back of a work the engine paused for returns sent back in a row, or a report marked as harming now, the one that came first; then the rest of the queue, the one that came first. A matter parked by a question the owner has not answered is not taken; nothing waits for the owner's reply.
steps.wait_to_start: No work exists yet: the engine takes this cell's rows for each item that waits, without a round, and the first that takes `ready` gets a work, which starts at the cell that row leads to. Of the items ready, one whose work was taken over starts first, since it waits only for a slot; then the projects with items ready take the free slots in turn, each in its architect's start order.
steps.wait_for_start: The agent paused: the engine pauses the work, tells the owner, and waits for the owner's Start; then the work goes back to the cell that paused, in the same session. This pause withdraws a resume that still waits for a free slot, as `resume_work` says. A work on an item that paused for its time budget also has its project's architect look at where it is stuck, as a place to set straight.
steps.bring_up: A work on an older flow version, when it next goes on with no step under way, is brought to the version the engine runs by what it carries now: where it stands, what rows recorded, the returns later cells will read and, in the middle of a cell, the session that cell has open. A new version ends a work when it has no graph for it, and an architect's work that can go on from none of its cells (below). The cell it serves is the one it is doing: where it stopped, else the first of the cells that wait for an answer, else the cell it stands at; it has begun that cell once a round ran there since the work last took a row of a cell that is not one of those every agent's cell shares (the tools, the owner's Start, the answers to who interjected) or of the asking part: a round that asked for tools and got their results, or a return sent back, has begun it, and coming to a cell, or standing at an engine's cell that has not run, has not. The returns later cells will read are the newest own answer of each cell the version reads from where the work stands, and the work's last return, which the cell after it reads by where it came from: the cells the work can still come to by the version's rows, from the cell it stands at and the cells it goes back to; each cell those cells read by its id, through an input's place or a database view that names it; and each cell the engine's own code reads by its id. An answer that no cell the work can still come to reads takes no part. An engineer's work whose merge stands (its merge cell took `merged`, and watching main has not taken `broken_by_merge` since) is judged by the rounds after its merge alone: only their returns count, only the cells they walked are gone back to, and only they are done again; its answers from before the merge take no part, later cells reading them as they are, so that neither the engine nor the owner's Start ever takes it back before its merge. Earlier returns of the cells every agent's cell shares and of the asking part are read only so, and are not counted. Each is compared by what its cell takes now, its outcome alone for an agent's, a field taking too what the flow names as it was earlier (`earlier`): absent, or in its shape then, which no return handed in now may be. It moves where it stands, in the same sessions, its version changed and no round recorded, when the version has the graph, every return counted still fits its cell, the cell it stands at is there, the cell it serves (and the agent's cell of the asking part whose session is open: the one it stands at, or the one whose tools are running) has not changed since it began it its kind, its line or the inputs of its own (their names and sources; those every agent's cell has come with what every return shares), and the cells it goes back to are there as cells of the same kind; a session in the middle of a cell is given what the version changed of its format, task and rows, and a return that does not fit them is sent back. Otherwise it comes here, its version changed, with where it goes back to as where it stopped: the first cell of the work's main way whose return does not fit, or the cell it serves when that changed or a cell it goes back to did not hold, or, when the cell it stands at or serves is gone, the latest cell it walked that the version has. It does that cell again from its start: the round it was in is cut off, the question it had out is withdrawn, as the cell that asked does it again, and what it answered, asked and was told stays. A work never goes back past a round that did what cannot be undone: an engineer's merge, once watching main took it back; and what an architect's round does at once: an action on a work or on new starts (a pause, a resume, a start over, new starts held or let go, an interjection), a word to the owner, a message to another project's architect, a change to observations, a reply that went out to an engineer or to the work that reported, and the item changes made. What has not taken effect is done again: what waits for a second eye is dropped, to be handed in again, its reply with it, the matters closed whose reply has not gone out go back to the queue, and the notebook is written again. An engineer's work that would go back past such a round stays here instead, paused, with the cell as where it stopped, for the owner to decide: the owner's Start takes it there all the same. When the version has none of the cells it walked, it stays here, paused, with nowhere to go back to: once a later flow version that has one is installed, the owner's Start looks again, a paused work not being brought to a new version until it goes on; one whose merge does not stand may be started over, or its item cancelled, meanwhile. An engineer's work that stays here asks its project's architect to set it straight, once for each version. An architect's work that would stay here ends instead, at once (`stop_architect_work`): it has no item to start over or cancel, and waiting here it would hold its project's architect for good. A work whose graph the version lacks ends, as no cell of the version can run it, and the owner is told why: an architect's work, or a policy setting's of a version before, leaves no hold of its project's new starts for setting it straight, and a policy setting's worktree is removed; an engineer's item gets a new work on the version, at once when a slot is free, else at the head of the queue.
steps.stop_work: A work cancelled, or started over by the owner or its project's architect, which a new work on the version the engine runs takes over, ends here from the cell it stands at, which it keeps as where it stopped. It ends once the step it is in has ended: a cancel or a start over is a request the engine's loop carries out then, and until then the owner's page shows the work stopping; while the engine does not run, the request waits for its next start. A round running when it is asked hands in nothing, and a round still open is cut off. A merge that came first stands, on main or still being made: the work is not cancelled or started over, whoever asked is told, and it goes on to watch main; the engine does not revert it, which is someone's decision. A work taken over leaves its worktree and pull request to the work that takes it over; if the item is cancelled before that work takes them up in its first cell, the cancel removes the worktree and closes the pull request.
steps.check_main: Checks main's red CI mechanically, holding the project's merge queue stopped: runs each red check again on the same commit, looks in the table of known red checks, and runs the red checks on main's commit before the merges since main was last green, in that order, and lists those merges. A later commit of main that is green clears it.

actions.answer_reporter: Tells the work that handed in the matter, a side report or a question, in one line to its engineer that needs no answer, what became of it, so that it does not report it again: the observation recorded or reported once more, or the items that took it in, by number and title; for a side report of which nothing was recorded, why; for a question, only what its reply does not say. As the round ends, or, when its changes wait for a second eye, once that finds them sound; a work that ended is told nothing.
actions.apply_effects: Carries out the effects of an answer, which the round's checks found sound: when none of its item changes is of a kind a second eye checks (a cancel, a merge, a split, a change that rewrites or removes an item's acceptance, a change on an item a work runs on), its item changes are made as the architect, in order, a key an earlier change made an item under given its number, and its changes to observations, actions and messages to other architects are made, each logged; otherwise everything it hands in waits for the second eye, made only once that finds it sound. A change to an item a work runs on that says why the work must change is said to that work.
actions.close_asks: Answers the work's open asks of the owner: no answer is needed, since the work ended.
actions.close_matter: Marks the matter in hand as handled by this round and ends its sessions, the fork's and the second eye's; once no place to set straight is left open, a hold of the project's new starts to set it straight is released.
actions.close_pr: Closes the work's pull request, when it never merged, saying only that its work ended without merging: why is in the owner's language, and a pull request is in English. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.deliver_answers: Sends each answer back to the side that interjected: to the owner's conversation, as the agent's message, or to the architect's queue as a report of the kind answer; and records it on the work: those of the answers form, those a redirect carries, and a cell's own answer to the owner's words.
actions.hand_over: Hands the task's blocker on to the holder of the cell the row passes the work on to, recording the move with why and what the holder that hands it on found: to a related project's architect, whose queue gets a matter saying which project and work it is for; the holder handing it on holds nothing then.
actions.hand_over_to_sub_items: Closes the work's draft PR, if any, saying which sub-items took over the work, as the architect's latest reply names them. The work does not merge; it waits for its sub-items.
actions.lock_new_acceptance: Writes the advisor's new acceptance conditions onto the item.
actions.open_session: The line of the cell the row goes to starts a new session there, at the cell's first round in the work: the session manager ends the one the line had going on.
actions.queue_followup: For a report: queues the latest what to do next the work handed in as a matter for the architect, with the report's paths under research/ and the commit the work merged.
actions.queue_for_architect: Queues each side report for the architect once; one that causes harm now (`harm_now`) is due at once, which starts a work of the architect when none runs, and when it comes while a work of the architect runs it is also given to that work at the top of its next round.
actions.queue_slots_free: When slots are free and fewer of a project's items are ready to start than slots are free, queues a matter of the kind slots_free for its architect, with how many slots are free and which items are ready, unless one waits already, new starts of the project are held (by the owner, by the architect, or to set the project straight), the owner has paused every work (none is queued then for any project, whether the owner started its architect or steps it, since no new work can start), the last was handled within the wait the configuration sets (`agents.slots_free_wait`), or the free slots and the items ready are those the last handled held.
actions.raise_blocker: Raises the task's blocker at the cell where its problem arose: an engineer's question, an engine tool's failure, an ask of the owner, a wait for items to deliver or for the owner's ruling, held by the holder of the cell the row leads to. A cell where the work waits raises it with its row that waits, for what it waits for.
actions.record_place: Records where the work runs, and the PR it keeps: every later round runs there, and each push is checked against the last pushed head.
actions.record_tool_runs: Records each run, the pushed head and the PR number under the calling cell.
actions.record_waits: Records the items the architect's reply has this work wait for, as parallel dependencies, since the work already runs. The engineer's session is kept, and the work holds no slot while it waits.
actions.release_straight_hold: New works of the project start again, if they were held to set it straight.
actions.remove_worktree: Removes the work's worktree; its branch stays. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.replace_design_cards: Marks the work's current decision cards replaced: the owner can no longer rule on them.
actions.resolve_blocker: Resolves the task's blocker with what its holder decided and did: the reply, the answer, or the items delivered.
actions.tell_owner: Puts each message the return tells the owner in the owner's interface, unread, and notifies the owner; the work goes on, and no answer comes back.
actions.tell_went_back: Tells the owner that the work went back to a cell of the new flow version, naming the round, the versions, the cell and why.
actions.report_stuck: Asks the project's architect, as a place to set straight, about the work that cannot go on in the new flow version, and why: once for each work and version, the same work found stuck again on that version asking nothing more, whether or not the architect handled the matter, and offering a work whose merge stands only the owner's Start once a version with a cell it walked is installed, as its merge refuses a start over and a cancel.
actions.wait_on_blocker: Counts the architect's time to act on the task's blocker again from now: the work chose to wait longer.
actions.withdraw_blocker: Withdraws the task's blocker, saying why, and tells its holder: its matter leaves the architect's queue, and its ask of the owner needs no answer.
actions.withdraw_blockers: Withdraws the open blocker of the work that ends, with the end's reason, and tells its holder; a resolution that comes for it later is recorded with it and moves nothing.
actions.withdraw_matters: Withdraws from the architect's queue what the work raised and still waits on it: its questions and its failures, saying why.
actions.queue_measures: Queues each new measure the signals of the policy that takes effect need, as the approved draft hands them in, as a matter of the kind set_straight, something missing, whose path makes an item that has the engine measure it; a measure the queue holds already is not queued again.
actions.queue_check_policy: Queues the check of whether the policy in force still holds, a matter of the kind check_policy, taken with what the plan queued, with why: what the cell's place given says. One open already, queued or parked for the owner's reply, stands instead, and takes the why. One asked for with no why of its own, as reading the project anew asks for it, is not queued while the policy in force and the constitution are those the last check handled had.
actions.ask_approval: Pins the engine's short question to the owner, whether the draft the round wrote is approved (Approve this policy? Reply exactly: approved), in the owner's one-to-one with the architect, as a question of the architect's that parks the matter in hand at the cell, without the draft; the draft is the round's return, which waits for the approval.
actions.write_learned: Adds what the work learned to its item's approach under `Learned:`, with the commits merged.
actions.tell_wait: Tells the owner once in the work, as it first takes the row: the engine cannot tell whether the installed program holds the work's merge, as its build's commit is unknown or not in the project's checkout. Only installing a build of main settles it; words said to the work buy one look, and the work waits again after it, up to the limit of the wait for an installation.
actions.report_verification: Queues what became of a work's checks after its change took effect as a matter for the project's architect, of the kind report: the item, the merge commit, the pull request and the result of each condition with the run that shows it, or that the change never took effect within the limit, or that the evidence never came within the limit of looks, each saying that the condition stands unverified. A condition that fails and is doing harm now (`harm_now`) makes the matter urgent, which the architect takes before what can wait.
actions.fresh_session: The line of the cell the row goes to starts a new session there, each time the work takes the row: the session manager ends the one the line had going on.
actions.record_acceptance: Writes the acceptance conditions of the plan or the design the work implements onto the item: the research's plan when the work goes straight to implement, the design the owner approved otherwise; later the implementation, a fix or the advisor may change them, saying why. If they are the same as those on the item, nothing changes.
actions.post_design_review: Queues the work's latest design, with what thinking again outside the frame examined, for the project's architect to review at the project's level, as an engineer's question of the kind design_review, which starts a work of the architect when none runs. The work does not wait for it: once the architect replied, the engine puts the design to the owner with the architect's comments, as an ask of the owner in the work's group of the kind design_review, and notifies the owner, who replies exactly approved to approve it, or says what to change and chooses an option for each decision point. An answer other than approved reaches the engineer as the owner's words. One queued already and not answered is not queued again.
actions.ask_owner_approval: Puts the change before the owner, as an ask of the owner in the work's group with the files the owner approves and the pull request to compare them on, and notifies the owner: reply exactly approved to approve it. The ask stands for the work's blocker; one put already and not answered is not put again.
actions.relay_owner_answer: Gives the owner's answer to the ask of the change, which was not exactly approved, to the work's engineer as the owner's words, which the way on chosen next takes in.
actions.apply_checked: Makes what the matter's session handed in and the second eye found sound: its item changes, its changes to observations, its actions and its messages, as `apply_effects` makes them; its reply goes, with the numbers of the items made, and the work that reported is told what became of it.
actions.return_checked: Sends what the matter's session handed in back to it, at the cell that handed it in, with what the second eye found: none of it takes effect, its reply does not go, and the session hands it in again, revised.
actions.queue_main_red: Watches main's CI for every project, at most once a minute each: when the full CI of main's latest commit has finished and a check that counts against a merge is red, and no matter of main red was queued for that commit, queues one, with the commit, the red checks and their runs. While a matter of main red is open, the project's merge queue is stopped: no work merges onto a red main.
actions.log_matter: Keeps the round's progress as the matter's record: the latest hand-in of the matter stands, and it reads as appended once the matter is handled.
actions.return_matters: What the architect's work that ends held and did not finish goes back to the project's queue, not handled, for the next work to take afresh: what waits for a second eye is dropped, its item changes marked revised and its reply held dropped, and the matters it closed whose reply has not gone out go back; the matter in hand goes back too, to start its path again, unless a cell of its path that hands in took effect, which closes it as handled by that round. Each matter that goes back or is closed so leaves its sessions, the fork's and the second eye's; one held by an ask of the owner keeps its session, to be taken up again with the answer.
actions.redo_matters: Undoes what the rounds the architect's work goes back to do again did that has not taken effect: what waits for a second eye is dropped, to be handed in again, and the matters they closed whose reply has not gone out go back to the queue, a reply held dropped, to be written again.
actions.keep_flow_feedback: Keeps the round's flow feedback where it is, in the round's return the engine keeps with the round, for the owner and the assistant to go through later. It goes to no agent's queue and starts nothing.
actions.ask_owner_points: Puts the decision points and the departures from decisions the research left before the owner, as one ask of the owner in the work's group of the kind points, and notifies the owner: the owner chooses an option for each and rules on each departure, or replies exactly approved to take what the research recommends. The work does not wait for it: it implements by the recommendation, and the merge gate waits for the answer. An answer other than approved reaches the engineer as the owner's words. Nothing when the research left none.
actions.ask_change_approval: Once the work's branch touches a path the project's configuration has the owner approve (`owner_approves`), and neither the owner's approval of its design nor an answer of approved covers the change, puts the change before the owner at once, as an ask of the owner in the work's group of the kind change, unless one waits for its answer: reply exactly approved to approve it. The work does not wait for it before the merge gate; another answer reaches the engineer as the owner's words, and the change is asked again.
actions.hold_for_approvals: Has the work's blocker at the merge gate stand for what the merge waits for: the architect's review of its design while the architect has not replied, then the owner's answer to the review, then the oldest ask of the decision points the research left that has no answer yet.
actions.write_understanding: Keeps the understanding the round handed in as the notebook's new understanding; the versions before stay, for the owner to look at.
actions.write_plan: Keeps the plan the round handed in as the notebook's new plan; the versions before stay, for the owner to look at.
actions.add_lines: Keeps the lines the round adds to the plan or the understanding with the matter's record: the latest hand-in of the matter stands.
actions.deliver_reply: Gives the reply to whoever the matter came from, by its kind: to the engineer waiting at its question, with the numbers of the items the round made in place of their keys, and with what the round's progress says when it wrote no reply, so that no engineer is left waiting; a reply that names an item no change made does not go out, and its matter goes back to the queue, not handled, with that reply and why, to be answered again. To the owner, as the architect's message in the conversation the words were said in, the group of the work they were said in, else the owner's one-to-one, and notifies the owner. To another project's architect, as a message in its queue. As the round ends, or, when its changes wait for a second eye, once that finds them sound.
actions.queue_steps: Withdraws the steps of the plan before not yet taken, and queues each step of this plan as a matter of the kind set_straight, taken in the plan's order, after what something waits on and before the rest of the queue, each in a session forked from this one.

checks.measure_matches_runs: An answer of measured has a run of this work's measure tool among the engine's records, a request that was refused not counting; any other answer (not_measured, from_records) has none. Reading the records, with query or otherwise, needs no run of measure.
checks.head_pushed_and_green: The head is the local HEAD, the worktree is clean, it was pushed with ci, and the latest fast CI run on it that ci made is green; so is the latest that ran tests, when a later run ran the lint only, which does not stand for them.
checks.branch_changes_fit_work: Against main, an implementation change has some change, otherwise the agent asks (another PR may have fixed it); a report changes nothing outside `research/`.
checks.checks_changed_known: Each check the change says it changes is one of the flow's `engine.checks`, named once, and neither this check nor `set_aside_answered`, which make the declaration no exemption and whose problems are never set aside; and the work's project is the one the engine is built from, whose changes alone can change the engine's checks. A declaration this check refuses holds nothing: what the checks it names find in the same return is sent back with it.
checks.in_effect_known: A condition written in_effect is one this project's work can check: `installed` only in the project the engine is built from, since no other project's change can change the installed program; and a work that delivers a report writes none, as nothing of it takes effect.
checks.verdicts_cover_in_effect: Each acceptance condition written in_effect has one verdict, and no other condition has one; `skipped` only once words were said to the work since its merge. How long to wait is there exactly when the look waits, a condition being not_yet and none failing, between one minute and two days.
checks.verdict_basis_ran: A verdict of holds or fails names the condition's own command, with the time the change took effect put in, as a run the engine recorded for this work since then, which ran and exited well; and what it says it saw is, letter for letter, a value of that run's rows, or part of a row holding one, or in a gh command's output, read from the file where a long result was saved.
checks.conditions_cover_acceptance: There is a row for each acceptance condition (at a re-check, each row names an existing condition), and a row of in_effect exactly for each condition written in_effect; each test named was reported by a run of ci on the pushed head, a name naming a test as the ci tool's tests say, and the tests none reported are named in the next ci, with the tests of the test table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; the report sections named are in the report.
checks.new_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing: each new-behaviour test this round's test changes add or extend (kind new_behaviour) has two results that match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; one red after the change or green before it is fixed in this round.
checks.guard_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing: each old-behaviour test this round's test changes add or extend (kind old_behaviour) has two results that match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; one red in either run is fixed in this round; one that cannot be built before the change (cannot_run) says why in `not_before`, and the details review judges it (the re-check, for one the fix added); one not run before the change is the details review's to judge.
checks.adversarial_test_results: Each row's two results match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; at a re-check, those red or disputed last time were run again; when tests were written, the head was pushed with ci.
checks.test_kinds_match: Tests the engineer added or extended, which adversarial testing lists as the engineer's, are in the table of the kind the engineer gave in the test changes. A test the adversarial tester wrote whose result before the change does not fit its kind is fixed in this round and run again; one not run before the change is the details review's to judge.
checks.tests_only: The commits from the head the engineer handed over to this head touch only the test paths the project's configuration names.
checks.fact_basis_ran: A basis of fact names a run the engine recorded, and its result is what that run gave.
checks.previous_findings_answered: At the re-check, there is a row for each row the latest fix answered, by its number, and none for another.
checks.set_aside_answered: Each finding set aside the round was given is answered once, by its number, and no other; one answered real names a finding of this return that carries it.
checks.table_answered: Every row of the table is answered once, with an answer the table allows for that row.
checks.no_disagreeing_after_insist: A finding the re-check insisted on is not answered disagree again; when neither side gives way, the engineer asks the advisor.
checks.not_caused_by_change: For a red check said not to be caused by the change, the engine checks it itself: the check is red on main as the worktree last fetched it, or in the table of known red checks; a flaky one is answered unrelated_flake. When main's checks cannot be read, it is taken as written.
checks.ruling_matches_advisor: This work did ask the advisor about this row, which ruled or had the architect or the owner rule in its place.
checks.answers_match_speakers: Each answer goes to a side that interjected in this round, one answer per side.
checks.departure_ruled_by_owner: A reply to an open question that says a design departs from a decision of its item that someone other than the architect made comes only once the owner has answered an ask that holds the question: only whoever made a decision rules on a departure from it. A reply that answers such a question says its ruling in departure (stands or turned_down); a reply to any other matter says none.
checks.policy_text_clean: The policy quotes none of the owner's words; it names no cell of the flow, no item and no date the owner said something.
checks.effects_valid: Every change and action holds, all its problems told at once. The change is well formed: an item named is there, or made by an earlier change of the round; a key is used once in the round; no item the round creates is cancelled in it; an item created has its title, problem, why, acceptance, level and deliverable; a title is within `items.title_max` and in the owner's language as far as its characters show it (for Chinese, Japanese or Korean, some character of East Asian wide width; for English, none); a split gives each acceptance condition to one new item at most; a dependency made is blocking or parallel; a dependency removed is one the items have then; after the round's dependencies and moves there is no cycle; an observation's tags are the project's; an observation merged into or closed is open; a work paused, resumed or interjected into is running; a message goes to another project's architect; no text of an item holds a line of a decision it did not hold, and a text that replaces an item's approach keeps every line of the item's decisions, letter for letter, in their order, under their head. The situation has not changed under it: an item it changes has not merged, nor been cancelled; a text it changes is at the version the change was drafted on; an acceptance it changes is not locked by a work's design; an item a work runs on is changed only by an answer to that work's own question, or with why the work must change; an observation it folds in was not folded into another item; a dependency it makes is not on an item merged, cancelled or held.
checks.reply_fits_changes: The reply names each sub-item and each item to wait for by its number or by the key a change of this round makes it under.
checks.learned_holds_no_decision: No line of the text starts a decision (`Decision (`): a decision is handed in as a decision, from the records it quotes, and the engine makes its line; what is learned holds facts and approaches dropped.
checks.holds_needs_policy: Once the owner replied to the question whether to research a new policy, the check of the policy hands in that it holds only while a policy is in force; with none, it writes the course the project keeps by the reply, or asks again.
checks.policy_or_kept: The writing of the policy hands in the whole policy with a draft written, or, with a draft kept, no policy and no new measures.
checks.asked_before_writing: The check of the policy hands in write_policy only once the owner said yes to a new policy: by the reply to the question whether to research one, or by the owner's own words, which asked for the check (queued by `H8`'s new_policy).
checks.ask_only_on_open_question: The ways for a question ask the owner only about an open question of an engineer's design, never about an engineer's question, whose engineer waits for the reply; and the question they pin links to the design it is about, as a markdown link to the link the matter holds.
checks.must_fix_fits_findings: The answer whether anything must be fixed is yes exactly when the first pass or the second found something.
checks.decisions_written: One row for each option the owner chose for a decision point at the review, by its number, none twice, and each file named is one the branch adds or changes under `decisions/` against main.

inputs.free_slots: The free slots, and the machines with room, as each machine's session manager reports.
inputs.project_guide: The project's AGENTS.md, and the index of its records (each file's path and first line), with the full text of the files the item cites.
inputs.local_commits: The bundle of the work's local commits the session manager made (git bundle).
inputs.review_base: What a review reviews, by commits the work's worktree has: main as fetched (`origin/<main>`), which is the pull request's base, the commit of main the branch was cut from or last took main in at, the head under review, the merges of main into the branch since it was cut (an empty list if it never took main in), the git command that reads the change between them, and at a re-review the head the last table review looked at with the merges since it.
inputs.tests_changed: The tests the engineer changed, from the test changes of every return of implementing and of fixing, oldest round first: `tests`, the latest added or extended row of each test that no later removal took away, each row as the engineer wrote it with the round it came from (it does not say whether the head still has the test: only a run of ci that names it says, and a name no test has gets a result of not_run with nothing matched); `weakened`, the latest removed, skipped and relaxed row of each test with its reason, a removed row dropped when the test was added again; `test_files`, the path of each file the work itself changed under the project's test paths (what merging main brought is left out), for the reader to find what changed in each in its diff, the tests the engineer did not name among them. A head git cannot read is said so as `unreadable`, with no `test_files`; none when the engineer changed no test and no test file was changed.
inputs.existing_work: What already exists for the item, as pointers to read: its earlier works here, with how far each got, why it ended and the queries that read their rounds, returns, decision cards and asks of the owner, and what each asked the architect and had withdrawn when it ended; where an imported item came from; the branch taken over, with the git commands that show what it adds beyond main; the PR kept, with the gh commands for its description, comments, reviews and checks.
inputs.constitution: The project's constitution, as its configuration names it.
inputs.guide: The project's guide as its main has it: its AGENTS.md, its design goal, and the index of its records.
inputs.numbers: The numbers the engine measures for the project, each up to the moment it is given and earlier, for the trend.
inputs.observation_tags: The project's set of tags for observations, each with what it covers.
inputs.policy: The policy in force for the project: its direction, why, its principles and the signals that the direction may have to change.
inputs.policy_signals: The signals of the project's policy the engine measures, each with its numbers: a signal that names a measure of the numbers by its name.
inputs.slots: The machines' slots, which every project shares: how many there are, used and free, and how many items are ready; and whether the engine runs works, the owner paused every work, with those that run despite it, or a failed run's cause stops every work.
inputs.matter: The matter in hand, with its material by its kind, and, for a question whose reply was not sent since an item it named was not made, that reply, the items it named that were made and why each other one was not.
inputs.similar_items: The items whose title or problem is close to those at hand, and the works under way whose branches changed the same paths.
inputs.owner_answer: The owner's answer to what was asked about the matter picked, when it comes back with one.
inputs.owner_talk: What was said in the project's one-to-one between the owner and its architect since the first round of the architect's previous session (the session of the project's latest understanding that was answered, across the works it ran in): each entry as the owner's page shows it, whole and oldest first, with when, who said it to whom and the words, an ask of the architect's with the owner's answer (counted as made when it was answered, if that was after the session began), and only how many images came with an entry. Before the project's first session there is no lower bound. Over 60,000 characters, the latest whole entries, then one line saying how many earlier ones there are; none when nothing was said since.
inputs.notebook_plan: The project's architect's plan as the latest round that planned wrote it, without what was added since; none before any did.
inputs.fix_table: The table the work's latest fix answered, as the fix was given it: each row with its number and what it held, a red check with its run and the end of its log.
inputs.set_aside: The findings set aside in this work that no review has judged yet: what the engine's checks found in a return of this work that only checks the work said it changes (`checks_changed`) found, recorded on the round instead of sending the return back. Each with its number in the work (S1, S2, ...), the check, the field it is about, its text, the round and that round's cell. A finding is judged once a round of the details review or of the re-check that came after it handed in its answer, which a finding in that round's own return is not; at the re-check, those that are rows of the table the fix answered are answered there and are not here. None when there are none.
inputs.new_tests: The engineer's tests of new behaviour with their two results, one row for each: read from the test changes of implementing and fixing (the rows added or extended with the kind new_behaviour), a test written again in a later round having its later row. Nothing is written back to a return.
inputs.guard_tests: The engineer's tests of old behaviour with their two results, one row for each: read from the test changes of implementing and fixing (the rows added or extended with the kind old_behaviour), a test written again in a later round having its later row. Nothing is written back to a return.
inputs.levels: The levels of the installation an item may be at, lowest first, each with its model and what work it is for.
inputs.history_sources: For the gatherer's git, the directory its own round runs in, a worktree of the project's repository, with the project's main as git has it there (`origin/<main>`).
inputs.effect: How the work's change took effect: its merge commit, when it merged and its pull request; for each acceptance condition written in_effect, what carries the change and that carrier's commit; whether all of them hold the merge now; and the time the change took effect (`at`, in milliseconds since the epoch): when cell `V1` first found them all holding it, or the merge's time before it has, which a command takes as `:in_effect_at`.
inputs.main_changes: Before the first round of cells `R1`, `D1` and `I1` each time the work comes to them, the engine merges the latest main into the work's branch when its worktree is clean: the files main changed since the branch last took it, or the files in conflict when it could not merge cleanly, the merge then undone; none when main changed nothing since.
inputs.decisions: The project's decisions in force, as its main has them at the commit the round is pinned to: every file of the directory its configuration names as decisions (decisions unless set) but a README.md, each by its path with its text; none when there are none. A decision a work writes or changes on its own branch is not here until it merges; it is in the work's diff.
inputs.owner_approval: The files of the work's change against main that match a path of the project's `owner_approves`, with the pull request and, for the flow, the flow page that compares it with main; whether the owner approved the work's design at its review, or replied exactly approved to the ask of this change since its last fix; none when the change touches none.
inputs.design_review: The review of the work's latest design: what the architect replied at the project's level, and the owner's answer with the images it sent, as cell `D3` brought them.
inputs.base_due: Whether a new base is due, and on what: the project has none, the policy changed since the base was built, or what came since it, in characters, against the installation's amount.
inputs.changes_to_check: The item changes of the matter in hand that wait for the second eye, numbered, each whole with its reason, and each item it touches in full, with the work running on it; at a look after a revision, which are new or changed since the second eye's last look.
inputs.handed_in: What the round that handed the changes in handed in besides them: its reply.
inputs.appended: What came since the project's base was built, oldest first: each matter handled, with its record and any line it added to the plan or the understanding; what the owner and the architect said to each other, whole; and what merged or was cancelled.
inputs.since_plan: What came since the plan before was written, as `appended` is worked out, for the round that writes the next plan: the base before is still the project's latest until that round ends.
